producer_report.summary: Root cause: the reader's brief never told it that a criterion for a loop (drain, queue), a protection or denial, or rendered output must name the real production path run end to end, its observable effect and a demonstration that the check can fail. Criteria therefore checked that parts existed. I added one `(prose only)` line to READING_RULES (13 to 14) with a Root cause comment citing the three jobs. No refusal check was added. I also added a test that the rendered brief carries the rule, updated the two length pins and the size bound in the existing reading-rules tests, and appended decision D184 and a CHANGELOG entry.

checks_run.note: applied formatting to briefs.rs; no separate `--check` run afterwards

criteria_check.criterion: crates/athena-context/src/briefs/reader.rs READING_RULES gains one new line, marked `(prose only)`, saying: for a loop-style command (drain, queue), protection or denial, or rendered or reported output, a behavior criterion names the real production path run end to end, the observable effect (for example an item landed, a record written, a page changed) and a demonstration that the check fails when the effect or guard is absent; the array length is updated to match. Preceded by a Root cause comment citing jobs 20261015-064153-wekz, 20261015-063409-hekk and 20261015-152305-6h8k.
criteria_check.evidence: Read reader.rs after the edit: the new line starts "Behavior:", ends "(prose only)." and the array type is [&str; 14]. The Root cause comment above it cites the three jobs. The wording is a shortened form of the criterion: "loop (drain, queue), protection or rendered output", "item landed, record written" and "a check that fails without it". It does not say "denial" or "page changed".

criteria_check.criterion: A new unit test in crates/athena-context/src/briefs.rs (or reader.rs tests) builds the reader brief and asserts it contains the new rule text; it fails on the code before the change. Verifier runs `cargo test -p athena-context`.
criteria_check.evidence: New test the_reader_brief_tells_the_reader_a_behavior_criterion_names_the_end_to_end_run_and_can_fail in briefs.rs finds the rendered "- Behavior:" line and asserts its key phrases. Before the change that line does not exist, so the `expect` panics. `cargo test -p athena-context` ran 151 passed, 0 failed.

criteria_check.criterion: No refusal check is added: `cargo test -p athena-core` still passes, including tests/refusal_corpus.rs unchanged, so expected 0% of newly refused readings; the rule is information only because giving the reader the information can prevent the failure.
criteria_check.evidence: No file under crates/athena-core changed, and the new line names no check function (the test asserts it has no "check_"). I did not run `cargo test -p athena-core` myself; Athena's full test run covers it. refusal_corpus.rs is unchanged.

criteria_check.criterion: A new appended entry in docs/decisions.md names the root cause (the reader was not told that criteria must check the end-to-end effect and that a check can fail), the alternatives (a refusal rule, rejected), and has a Provenance bullet; CHANGELOG.md records the change. No existing entry is edited.

The rule line covers the loop, protection and rendered-output patterns generically. The three jobs are named in the Root cause comment, in D184 and in the CHANGELOG entry, and `intro.json` is not named.

learnings: The reading-rules size test in briefs.rs pins the section to a 3045-byte baseline plus the field-meaning line, with a hard 3300-byte limit. A new rule line has to update both.
The rule line must be at most 220 bytes including the leading "- ", or the one-short-line test fails.
